To address the issue of image elements not having explicit `width` and `height` attributes, we need to modify the code to ensure these attributes are set. This will help reduce layout shifts and improve the Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) metric.

### Bug Scenario and Root Cause

The bug scenario involves image elements in a report that do not have explicit `width` and `height` attributes. This can lead to layout shifts as the browser does not know the dimensions of the images beforehand. The images are currently hotlinked from a remote server, and the goal is to replace them with full-page screenshots to simplify content security policy (CSP) and mixed content issues.

### Bug Location and Fix

We need to modify the code in `lighthouse-core/gather/gatherers/image-elements.js` to ensure that images have explicit `width` and `height` attributes. This involves setting these attributes based on the natural dimensions of the images.

### Patches

Here are the patches to fix the issue:

```javascript
### lighthouse-core/gather/gatherers/image-elements.js
<<<<<<< SEARCH
      attributeWidth: element.getAttribute('width'),
      attributeHeight: element.getAttribute('height'),
=======
      attributeWidth: element.getAttribute('width') || element.naturalWidth,
      attributeHeight: element.getAttribute('height') || element.naturalHeight,
>>>>>>> REPLACE
```

This change ensures that if the `width` and `height` attributes are not explicitly set, they will default to the natural dimensions of the image. This will help prevent layout shifts and improve the CLS metric.
